etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English hen, from Old English henn (“hen”), from Proto-West Germanic *hannju, from Proto-Germanic *hanjō (“hen”), from Proto-Indo-European *kan-, *kana- (“to sing”).

Cognate with Saterland Frisian Hanne (“hen”), West Frisian hin (“hen”), Dutch hen (“hen”), German Low German Heen (“hen”), German Henne (“hen”), Danish høne (“hen”), Swedish höna (“hen”), Icelandic hæna (“hen”). Related to Old English hana (“cock, rooster”). Also cognate to Latin cicōnia (“stork”), Latin canō (“to sing”), Russian каню́к (kanjúk, “buzzard”). Compare Russian пету́х (petúx, “rooster, cock”) from Russian петь (petʹ, “to sing”).

definitions.definition: A female chicken (Gallus gallus), particularly a sexually mature one kept for her eggs.

quote.citation: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter II, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: She was a fat, round little woman, richly apparelled in velvet and lace,  […] ; and the way she laughed, cackling like a hen, the way she talked to the waiters and the maid, […]—all these unexpected phenomena impelled one to hysterical mirth, and made one class her with such immortally ludicrous types as Ally Sloper, the Widow Twankey, or Miss Moucher.

definitions.definition: A female of other bird species, particularly a sexually mature female fowl.

quote.citation: 2023 June 17, Severin Carrell, “Dancing Capercaillie bird makes a tentative comeback in Scotland”, in The Guardian‎[6]:
quote.text: In Tain, north of Inverness, staff detected 11 males and at least seven hens – the highest number there since 2011.

definitions.definition: (uncommon) A female fish (especially a salmon or trout) or crustacean.

quote.citation: 2005, Roderick Sutterby, Malcolm Greenhalgh, “Life in the Nursery”, in Atlantic Salmon: An Illustrated Natural History, Mechanicsburg, PA: Stackpole Books, →ISBN, page 21:
quote.text: As spawning time approaches – autumn or very early winter in most rivers, though in some late-run streams salmon may spawn as late as January or February – the hen's colouration becomes first a matt-pewter and then a drab dark brown-grey. The cock fish, in contrast, begins to gain some brighter colours.

definitions.definition: (UK, informal) A bride-to-be, particularly in the context of a hen night.

quote.citation: 1785, Francis Grose, A Classical Dictionary of the Vulgar Tongue:
quote.text: Hen, a woman. A cock and hen club; a club composed of men and women.

definitions.definition: (Scotland, informal) An affectionate term of address used to women or girls.
(transgender slang) The penis of a trans woman.
(figuratively, derogatory, uncommon) A henlike person of either sex.
The hard clam (Mercenaria mercenaria), a bivalve shellfish.
(obsolete) A large pewter pot used in a tavern.

quote.text: Once he had flared up, "If ever a man was henned, it's me!"

quote.citation: 1984, Susan C. Feldhake, Love Beyond Surrender, page 52:
quote.text: Mammy henned the black workers into placing the trunks beside the girls.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English henne, heonne, hinne, from earlier henene, heonenen, henen, from Old English heonan, hionan, heonane, heonone (“hence, from here, away, from how”), from Proto-Germanic *hina, *hinanō (“from here”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱe-, *ḱey- (“this, here”). Cognate with Dutch heen (“away”), German hin (“hence, from here”), Danish hen (“away, further, on”). See also hence.
From hen (“hence, away”), or a variant of hench.
